newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Woolworths says petrol business a gas.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Woolworths says petrol business a gas.

text.p: Woolworths Ltd said on Monday it was very pleased with the progress of the petrol outlets it is trialing at six of its supermarkets.

"The first six that we have put down have varied in turnover. Certainly the performance in all those six has been beyond our original projections so we are very happy with it and will continue to roll them out as quickly as possible," said the head of Woolworths supermarket division, John Brunton.
Brunton said Woolworths had another 40 sites that had been approved or were in the process or being approved and an additional 100 sites were on the drawing board.
Woolworths has an agreement with Burmah Oil to sell refined petroleum product from some Woolworths outlets in New South Wales and Victoria.
Woolworths has watched closely the success of Tesco Plc's petrol retailing operations in Britain.

British supermarkets increased their share of the petrol market to 20-25 percent by discounting, as they can cover potential losses on petrol at least in part by added grocery sales created as customers make one stop for all their shopping.
Woolworths said in November last year it aimed to achieve a one percent increase in sales from its shopping centres because of the linked petrol outlets.
